 Miles McBride produced 20 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and six three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics.
 McBride rebounded nicely from his poor showing in Tuesday’s loss to the 76ers, a game in which he scored three points on 1-of-5 shooting. Against the Celtics, Deuce shot 6-of-8 from three and scored 20 of the Knicks’ 32 bench points. The reserve role doesn’t help McBride deliver consistent fantasy value, but he can be an effective source of points and three-pointers in deep leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 OG Anunoby (hamstring) is probable to play against the Cavaliers on Tuesday. 
 Anunoby missed Games 3 and 4 of the Knicks’ series against the 76ers, but he is expected to return to take on Cleveland. This doesn’t come as a surprise after he was a full participant in practice last week. Miles McBride replaced him in the starting lineup but will head back to the bench with Anunoby likely to return. 
 OG Anunoby 
 NYK 
 Forward-Guard 
 #8 
 ESPN’s Vincent Goodwill reports that the Knicks are optimistic that OG Anunoby (hamstring) will be ready for Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Finals. 
 After sweeping Philadelphia in the conference semifinals, the earliest that the Knicks will play again is on Sunday, May 17. Anunoby has been out since suffering a minor strain of his right hamstring during the latter stages of Game 2 of the conference semifinals and has not played since. He has been limited to individual work in recent practices, but there’s reportedly optimism that the forward will be ready for Game 1. If Detroit can force a Game 7, the conference finals would not begin until May 19, which would mean 13 days to recover for Anunoby. Miles McBride has been the replacement in the starting lineup, and he made seven three-pointers in the series-clinching Game 4 rout of the 76ers. 
 Miles McBride 
 NYK 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Miles McBride tallied 25 points (7-of-10 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, one steal and seven three-pointers in Sunday’s Game 4 win over the 76ers. 
 After offering limited production as OG Anunoby’s replacement in the starting lineup for Game 3, McBride was outstanding in Sunday’s series clincher. Deuce shot 7-of-9 from beyond the arc, sinking one fewer three pointer than the 76ers did as a team. McBride led the Knicks in scoring, while Landry Shamet contributed 12 points and four three-pointers in 11 minutes off the bench. What their roles will be in the conference finals depends on Anunoby’s hamstring, which he strained late in Game 2.

 OG Anunoby (hamstring) is questionable for Sunday’s Game 4 against the 76ers. 
 Injured during the fourth quarter of the Knicks’ Game 2 victory, Anunoby did not play in Friday’s win that gave New York a 3-0 series lead. Miles McBride moved into the starting lineup, and Anunoby’s absence also meant more opportunities for Landry Shamet, who scored 15 points off the bench. Look for those two to continue in those roles for Game 4 if Anunoby remains out. 
 Landry Shamet 
 NYK

 Landry Shamet recorded 15 points (5-of-6 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, one steal and two three-pointers in Friday’s Game 3 win over the 76ers. 
 On a night when the Knicks were without OG Anunoby (hamstring), Shamet stepped up with his most productive game of these playoffs. He didn’t start Game 3, with Miles McBride (three points, two assists, two blocks and one three-pointer) receiving the nod, but Shamet was more productive and logged 27 minutes to Deuce’s 21. With New York now leading the series three games to none, there’s little need for them to force anything regarding Anunoby’s hamstring. Don’t be surprised if they stick with the same rotation of McBride and Shamet for Game 4.

 According to ESPN’s Shams Charania, OG Anunoby (hamstring) is considered day-to-day. 
 Anunoby injured his right hamstring during the fourth quarter of Wednesday’s Game 2 win over the 76ers. He has since been diagnosed with a strain and will be considered day-to-day, with a questionable tag for Friday’s Game 3. If Anunoby can’t play, Miles McBride and Mitchell Robinson are potential replacements in the starting lineup.

 NYK 
 Forward-Guard 
 #8 
 OG Anunoby (hamstring) finished Wednesday’s Game 2 win over the 76ers with 24 points (9-of-17 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, four steals, one block and two three-pointers. 
 Anunoby has been on a roll recently, with his play among the reasons the Knicks have looked like the team best equipped to come out of the East. However, there is now a serious injury concern, as the versatile forward pulled up lame and asked out of Wednesday’s victory with about three minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. Anunoby was seen reaching for his right hamstring, and while the team had no information after the game, this is a concern. Anunoby suffered a strained hamstring during Game 2 of the Knicks’ 2024 second-round series against the Pacers, with his return for Game 7 lasting a few minutes before needing to exit. Miles McBride, Mitchell Robinson and Landry Shamet are potential replacements in the starting lineup if Anunoby has to miss time.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo had 36 points (15-of-26 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Pistons. 
 Antetokounmpo has now had at least 35 points in each of his first two games in a Heat uniform. He played a more complete game across the stat sheet compare to the opener with 12 rebounds, five assists and three stocks. Still, the Heat lost to the Pistons by 17 after dropping the opener to the Timberwolves by 25. Miami will look for its first win of the season and probably get it against the reeling Hornets in Charlotte on Saturday.

 Duncan Robinson had 17 points (5-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, two assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Heat. 
 Robinson is yet to make a two-point field goal so far this season, but he’s 10-of-19 from behind the three-point line in the first two games this year. The 32-year-old forward’s fantasy utility is mostly limited to his three-point shooting, but it looks like the right time to continue to ride the hot hand.

 John Collins had 23 points (9-of-15 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers against the Heat on Friday. 
 Collins had a quiet debut with six points in the win over the Celtics on Tuesday, but he was excellent in the win over the Heat on Friday. The 29-year-old power forward was 9-of-15 from the field, including 5-of-6 from behind the three-point line. Jalen Duren (thigh) left with an injury in the second quarter and didn’t return, which likely led to more opportunities for Collins. With Duren’s status still up in the air, Collins could be in line for more usage again on Sunday against the 76ers. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Cade Cunningham had 16 points (5-of-8 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, eight assists, one steal, three blocks and two three-pointers in the Pistons’ 128-111 victory over the Heat on Friday. 
 Cunningham had another fine game as he filled the stat sheet and led the Pistons to another win to start the season. However, after turning the ball over five times in the win over the Celtics on Tuesday, he had seven turnovers against the Heat on Friday. Even opposing coaches like the Heat’s Erik Spolstra have pointed out that Cunningham isn’t necessarily a bad ball-handler, but commits a lot of turnovers thanks to almost always having the ball in his hands. That doesn’t offer much comfort to fantasy managers with Cunningham in nine-category leagues as he’s likely to be towards the top of the league in turnovers this year. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Brandon Miller had six points (2-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Hawks on Friday. 
 There’s no sugarcoating it; Miller is off to a rough start to begin the season. The 23-year-old small forward had 18 points in the opener, but shot just 7-of-21 from the floor. He followed that performance up by going 2-of-14, including 1-of-11 from behind the three-point line. He’s now 4-of-25 (16 percent) from behind the arc to begin the season. Miller was an almost incomprehensible -37 in 22 minutes in the 128-81 loss to the Haws Friday. Is this rock bottom? Because it feels like it can only get better from here. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Reid had seven turnovers despite only playing 24 minutes and that’s a crusher in nine-category leagues. Otherwise, he’s scored 37 points on 15-of-34 attempts with seven three-pointers in his first two games with the Hornets. That’ll play. If Reid can keep the turnovers under control, he’s well on his way to paying off his mid-round draft price.

 Brunson’s gotten off to a slow start by his standards, shooting 13-of-32 from the field in New York’s first two games.  Jalen Johnson had 19 points (9-of-16 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), seven rebounds, eight assists, three steals and one block in Friday’s game against the Hornets. 
 With less than two minutes left in the first half, Dyson Daniel hit the floor for one of his seven steals, leading to a Jalen Johnson alley-oop dunk on the other end. That pretty much encapsulates how the night went for the Hawks as Johnson led the team in scoring with 19 in the 128-81 blowout win. Johnson showed he was able to move past the extracurriculars with the Magic on Wednesday with his usual excellent performance against the Hornets.
